=== FINDINGS FROM deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro ===
- tests/test_workflow_failure_heal.py | severity=high | confidence=4
  PROBLEM: The comment "Jobs can be listed even when the job-log endpoint returns 404" describes the situation correctly: `job_logs={}` empties only job logs while the `_plan_intake_state` jobs dict (`{"500": [{"id": 9101, ...}]}`) remains populated. The mock at line 912-919 serves jobs from `state["jobs"][run_id]`, so the intake writes a valid `PHASE_JOBS_FILE` in its log-collection loop. The provenance verifier should see that file and pass (`verified=True`). But the assertion expects `skip reason=phase_report_unverified detail=jobs_unavailable`. Either the comment is stale and the assertion reflects a regression where an empty job-log dict accidentally prevents the jobs file from being written, or the assertion itself is wrong and provenance should pass — the two conflict.
  WHY: If the assertion is correct (provenance fails despite available jobs), then empty job logs silently prevent verification and every phase report whose job logs happen to be unavailable is dropped. If the assertion is wrong, the test will fail when run against the real intake script because provenance will pass instead of returning `jobs_unavailable`.

=== END FINDINGS FROM deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro ===

=== FINDINGS FROM google_gemini-3_1-flash-lite ===
- scripts/workflow_failure_heal_intake.sh: line 294, line 316 | severity=critical | confidence=4
  PROBLEM: The provenance verification incorrectly requires the GitHub comment author to match the intake repository's pipeline identity, rather than validating that the author is an authorized member or bot of the source repository itself.
  WHY: Consumer repositories are intended to use their own configured GH_PAT secrets for dispatching workflows. When a consumer uses their own authorized account, the comment author will not match the intake repository's account identity. Consequently, the intake verifier rejects all legitimate phase-failure reports from consumer repositories with untrusted_comment_author, effectively breaking the healing functionality for all documented consumer configurations.
- tests/test_workflow_failure_heal.py | severity=low | confidence=4
  PROBLEM: The test comment suggests jobs can be listed even when the job-log endpoint returns 404, but the assertion expects jobs_unavailable, even though the jobs fixture is populated.
  WHY: The comment and test expectation contradict the actual implementation logic in the provenance verifier. If jobs exist, they should be returned, not marked unavailable, unless the verifier logic has an undocumented dependency on job-log availability.

=== END FINDINGS FROM google_gemini-3_1-flash-lite ===

=== FINDINGS FROM qwen_qwen3_7-plus ===
- scripts/workflow_failure_heal_intake.sh:294 | severity=high | confidence=4
  PROBLEM: The intake validates the linking comment against its own GH_PAT identity, but consumer repositories use their own separately configured GH_PAT secret. When the accounts differ (the typical consumer setup), every legitimate phase-failure report is rejected with untrusted_comment_author.
  WHY: A consumer repo with its own GH_PAT posts a failure comment using that token. The intake fetches its own identity (coding-workflows' GH_PAT login). The verifier requires comment.user.login == trusted_author. The two logins do not match, the report is dropped, and a Telegram WARNING fires for every real failure. The README documents this requirement ("The reporter and intake must use the same account for GH_PAT") but this breaks the documented consumer configuration where each repo has its own GH_PAT. The security improvement becomes an availability regression for the typical setup.
- tests/test_workflow_failure_heal.py:3816-3820 | severity=high | confidence=4
  PROBLEM: The test comment says "Jobs can be listed even when the job-log endpoint returns 404" but the assertion expects skip reason=phase_report_unverified detail=jobs_unavailable. When only job_logs={} is passed, the jobs dict remains populated from _plan_intake_state's default. The provenance verifier checks jobs, not job_logs, so the jobs API mock should return the jobs list and provenance should pass.
  WHY: The comment and assertion contradict each other. Either the test expectation is wrong (provenance should pass and the test should check fingerprinting behavior), or the intake script has an undocumented dependency where jobs-file population fails when job logs are unavailable.
- README.md:1519-1520 | severity=high | confidence=4
  PROBLEM: This introduces a new requirement that the reporter and intake use the same GH_PAT account. This is a backward compatibility break for the documented consumer setup where each repository has its own GH_PAT secret.
  WHY: Consumers configured per the existing documentation (each repo with its own GH_PAT) will suddenly have all phase-failure reports rejected. The security audit finding asked to "bind each reporter credential to its authorized source repository" but the implementation binds to the intake's identity instead, which is a different and more restrictive requirement. This breaks the existing consumer contract without a migration path or opt-out.
- TASK_GAP
  Requirement: "bind each reporter credential to its authorized source repository"
  Expected change site: scripts/workflow_failure_heal_intake.sh or scripts/workflow_failure_heal.py
  Evidence of absence: The implementation binds the comment author to the intake's GH_PAT identity (PHASE_COMMENT_AUTHOR from the intake's /user call) rather than binding the reporter credential to the source repository. The linked issue asks for repository-level binding, but the implementation uses identity-level binding. The AD-3 decision in the PR description acknowledges this ("per-sender binding would add little beyond verifying evidence in the claimed repository") but the issue explicitly asks for reporter credential binding to the source repository, which is not implemented.
  SEVERITY: MAJOR
  ISSUE_CONFIDENCE: 3

=== END FINDINGS FROM qwen_qwen3_7-plus ===

=== FINDINGS FROM z-ai_glm-5_2 ===
- scripts/workflow_failure_heal.py:408-416 | severity=high | confidence=5
  PROBLEM: The last run tightened the linking-comment check to require the comment author to match the intake's own GH_PAT identity (`trusted_author`, resolved at workflow_failure_heal_intake.sh:294 via `gh api user`). But the phase failure comments are posted by the phase workflows running in the consumer repo, which use the consumer's `secrets.GH_PAT` — a different account. See plan.yml:2314-2327 (`GH_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.GH_PAT }}` then `gh api .../comments -f body=$'AI planning workflow failed...'`) and implement.yml:5523-5586 (same pattern). The intake runs in coding-workflows and resolves coding-workflows' GH_PAT identity. For any consumer repo that uses its own GH_PAT (the documented and typical setup per README secrets table), the comment author will never match `trusted_author`, and every legitimate `phase_failure` report is dropped with `untrusted_comment_author` (or `comment_author_unavailable` if the identity read fails). The heal intake becomes an availability regression for the exact consumer-repo configuration it is designed to serve. The pre-last-run code accepted any comment from a trusted association (OWNER/MEMBER/COLLABORATOR) or a trusted bot login, which was correct: an attacker would need to be a trusted collaborator in the target repo to post the linking comment, at which point they already have repo access. The README documents the constraint ("The reporter and intake must use the same account for GH_PAT") but this is not an operational expectation the consumer setup enforces or even surfaces during onboarding.
  WHY: A consumer repo's plan run fails. The plan workflow posts "AI planning workflow failed" on the source issue using the consumer's GH_PAT (e.g. account `consumer-ci`). The heal-report job dispatches to coding-workflows. The intake resolves `PHASE_COMMENT_AUTHOR=coding-workflows-ci`. The verifier checks `comment.user.login == "coding-workflows-ci"` against a comment authored by `consumer-ci` — mismatch — returns `untrusted_comment_author` — the report is dropped and a Telegram WARNING fires for every real failure.

=== END FINDINGS FROM z-ai_glm-5_2 ===
